This page lists the forms in MAM's documentation notes that use plus notation or double guillemets.

In plus notation, two sets of marks on one letter are shown by writing the letter twice, joined by a plus sign, with one set of marks on each copy.

MAM-basics' near-Aleppo example edition has some marks on an artificial carrier letter between double guillemets (« »). MAM's notes sometimes quote a form between single guillemets (‹ ›); those are different characters and do not count here.

# double-guillemets: None are found.

# plus: Immediately below, all 8 are shown.

זֶ֠+ז֞ה G5:29
רְאוּבֵ֔+ב֗ן G35:22
תִּֿרְצַ֖+צָֽח E20:12
שֻׁ֠+ש֜בוּ 2K17:13
[אֵ]שֵ֥נַיְ+יֵהֶ֖ם 2K18:27
וּ֜+וּ֠לְאֵלֶּה Ee48:10
וּ֜+וּ֠לְאֵ֜לֶּה Ee48:10
זֹ֠+ז֞את Ts2:15
